$doc: Vyomi capability registry — Azure AI services / Cognitive Services. See azure/keyvaults.json for the contract.

azure.cognitiveservices.account.crud.title: Accounts (create, get, list, update, delete) over ARM — every kind in core/azure_cognitiveservices_core.py KINDS

azure.cognitiveservices.keys.title: Keys and Endpoint (listKeys, regenerateKey)
limitations: Keys are deterministic simulator secrets, not material an inference call is checked against — any non-empty bearer value is accepted by the (non-simulated) data plane. regenerateKey changes the stored value and is honest about which of Key1/Key2 it rotated.

azure.cognitiveservices.deployments.title: Model deployments (create, get, list, delete) over ARM — Azure OpenAI and Azure AI services kinds
limitations: Deployment, quota and rate-limit bookkeeping (capacity, Tokens-Per-Minute quota per model) is real; the model itself is not served — Vyomi has no local inference backend, so the deployment's data-plane chat/completions/embeddings endpoint is not simulated (console-only: control plane CRUD).
Deployments are only accepted on OpenAI and AIServices kind accounts, matching the real service; other kinds return the native InvalidParameter error, same as Azure.

azure.cognitiveservices.quotas.title: Quotas (usages: per-model Tokens-Per-Minute for OpenAI/AIServices, TotalCalls for every other kind)

azure.cognitiveservices.networking.title: Networking (public network access / firewall default action)
limitations: publicNetworkAccess and networkAcls round-trip through ARM exactly as written, but Vyomi does not enforce them against the account's Keys and Endpoint or Model deployments calls — unlike azure.keyvaults.networking, this data plane has no per-account routing signal to check (no x-vyomi-account equivalent is wired into core/aws_wire_router.py for Microsoft.CognitiveServices yet).

azure.cognitiveservices.identity.title: System-assigned managed identity
limitations: System-assigned identity (principalId/tenantId) is real and persists across PATCH. User-assigned managed identities are an honest 'Not simulated' gap — Microsoft.ManagedIdentity/userAssignedIdentities is not a catalogued resource type in Vyomi, so there is nothing to attach.

azure.cognitiveservices.locks.title: Resource locks (Microsoft.Authorization/locks), scoped to this account
limitations: Locks are only simulated at the resource scope (this account); subscription- and resource-group-scoped lock lists are an honest 'Not simulated' gap, same as the real Subscription/Resource group scope-switch buttons.

azure.cognitiveservices.activity_log.title: Activity log
limitations: Only console/SDK-triggered mutations made since the simulation booted are recorded (no historical backfill), and `caller` is a fixed placeholder identity rather than the real signed-in principal. Severity/category filtering is not modelled (every recorded event is Informational/Administrative).

The Timespan picker IS enforced: its lower bound is a real OData `eventTimestamp ge` predicate (core/azure_arm_core.py _activity_log_query) — narrowing it really narrows the result, it isn't a cosmetic control.

azure.cognitiveservices.soft_delete.title: Soft-delete, restore and purge (deletedAccounts)
limitations: There is a fixed soft-delete retention window applied by the engine rather than a configurable per-account retention policy (Cognitive Services accounts have no 'purge protection' toggle in real Azure either, unlike Key vaults).

azure.cognitiveservices.iam.title: Access control (IAM)
limitations: Check access, Role assignments and Deny assignments are REAL and scoped to this Cognitive Services account's resource id: Check access runs core/azure_iam_core.py's evaluator (explicit-deny-wins, scope inheritance from the subscription/resource group), the lists filter the shared RBAC store to assignments whose scope covers it, and new assignments are created scoped to it. Principal IDs are free text (Vyomi has no real directory); 'My access' and Classic administrators stay honest gaps.
